sections.overview: Porcellio albinus is a desert-adapted terrestrial isopod studied in southern Tunisia.
sections.identification: It is a woodlouse in the family Porcellionidae; the sources consulted focus on ecology rather than a field identification key.
sections.habitat: It occupies arid and Saharan regions of North Africa, including sandy habitats in southern Tunisia; records also extend to the Canary Islands and Niger Sahara.
sections.diet: The species-specific diet is not detailed in the studies consulted.
sections.behavior: It is a burrowing, mainly nocturnal species; surface activity varies with time of day and season in the Tunisian desert population studied.
sections.reproduction: A field study in Zarat found seasonal breeding, with two breeding periods during the year; this result is specific to that population.
sections.ecology: It is adapted to sandy desert soils. Unlike P. albinus, P. dilatatus is often found around human settlements.
sections.conservation: The ecological studies consulted do not give a global conservation assessment for this species.
